system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
Jay has to draw a shape.
- It must have 5 sides.
- It must have one line of symmetry.
Jay has started to draw the shape.
Complete Jay’s shape.

[Image: an incomplete shape with three sides forming a rectangle on a grid.]

Figure, described in words:
A 10 by 10 square grid. A three-sided incomplete shape is drawn with thick black lines along the grid lines: a horizontal bottom segment 6 units long (leaving 2 units of margin on the left and 2 units on the right along the bottom edge of the grid), and two vertical segments each 4 units tall rising upward from the two ends of the bottom segment (leaving 6 units of grid space above them). The top of the shape is open.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer:
To complete the shape, draw two line segments that meet at a single point to form the roof of a house:

1. Find the vertical line of symmetry, which is the vertical grid line exactly halfway between the two vertical sides (3 units from the left side and 3 units from the right side).
2. Choose a point on this vertical line of symmetry above the two open ends (for example, 3 units above the top ends of the sides, on the center line).
3. Draw a straight line segment connecting the top of the left vertical side to this chosen center point.
4. Draw a straight line segment connecting the top of the right vertical side to the same center point.

This adds 2 sides to the existing 3 sides, creating a 5-sided shape (a pentagon) with one vertical line of symmetry.
